clue.text: Voyeurs tweeting closed M&S

blocks.note: chicks peep, a small high cry like a bird's tweet
a door pushed to is closed
the letters of M&S with the ampersand dropped

explanation.surface: Peeping toms have been posting online about a shut-down branch of the Marks & Spencer chain.
explanation.walkthrough: M&S is Marks & Spencer, a British department store. 'Tweeting' suggests social media, but it is a bird call.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeping Toms are people who secretly watch others undressing, the classic everyday name for voyeurs.

clue.text: Judge probes Eastern European dodge

indicators.note: something that probes pushes its way inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for Eastern
from m'lud, the courtroom address to a judge
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A magistrate is investigating how someone from eastern Europe evaded something.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to escape or evade by cunning, the same verb sense as to dodge.

clue.text: Local building lacking support for important part of development

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so some letters are taken out of the building word

blocks.note: the local is a Briton's neighbourhood pub
a building is a property
a prop is a support

explanation.surface: A pub building lacks a structural support, which matters for a property development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development' suggests property building, but the definition is about human growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Puberty is the stage of sexual maturing, a crucial phase in a young person's growth.

clue.text: Support for board ousting trustee in favour of new food company

indicators.note: ousting means throwing out, so one part of the support word is removed
in favour of names what is put in place of the ousted part

blocks.note: a trestle holds up a board to make a table
tr. is a dictionary abbreviation for trustee
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A company board ousts one trustee in favour of a newcomer at a food firm.
explanation.walkthrough: TR at the front of TRESTLE is swapped for N. 'Board' looks corporate, but it is a plank on a trestle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestlé is the Swiss multinational behind KitKat and Nescafé, an example of a food company.

clue.text: Rip-off ruffian

blocks.note: first meaning: ..., to pull something off by ripping
second meaning: a reckless, unruly young person

explanation.walkthrough: Rip-off reads as a swindle, but it is the verb rip off, split as TEAR AWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a wild, uncontrollable youngster, close to a ruffian; to tear away is to pull off forcibly.

clue.text: Jonah crashes in car game

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the prophet's name is jumbled
in places the jumbled letters inside the car

blocks.note: MG is a British sports car make
taken as written

explanation.surface: Jonah has a car accident while out driving.
explanation.definitionFit: Mah-jong is the Chinese tile game for four players, so it is a game by example.

clue.text: Include gnomes on lively prime time saga

indicators.note: lively means animated and bouncing about, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wants garden gnomes added to a lively television drama series at peak viewing.
explanation.walkthrough: Gnomes here are not garden ornaments but gnomic sayings, short pithy maxims.
explanation.definitionFit: To epigrammatise is to put things in short witty sayings, and gnomes are such maxims, so it means working them in.

clue.text: Figures from station finally covered by a railway

indicators.note: with its end covered up, the last letter of the word can no longer be seen

blocks.note: one's station in life is one's status
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Statues at a station end up sheltered by a railway company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Station' looks like a railway stop, but it means social rank; STATUS loses its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuary is statues collectively, so it means sculpted figures.

clue.text: What a violent bounder might do when hopping mad!

definitions.text: What a violent bounder might do when hopping mad!

blocks.clueFragment: What a violent bounder might do
blocks.note: surface reading: a cad in a rage behaves badly
setter's reading: a bounder is something that bounces, and jumping hard enough sends it up to the room's top surface; the idiom means flying into a rage

explanation.walkthrough: Bounder is old British slang for a cad, but here it is literally one that bounds, and hopping is literal too.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for becoming furiously angry pictures someone leaping so high their head strikes the overhead surface.

clue.text: Measure lead Scottish smoker inhaled

indicators.note: what is inhaled is drawn inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
lum is the Scots word for a chimney, which smokes

explanation.surface: A Scottish smoker breathing in lead fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoker' suggests a person with a cigarette, but it is a chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb is to sound or gauge depth, originally with a lead weight on a line, so it means to measure.

clue.text: The pigs ate endless processed food

indicators.note: endless means without an end, so the last letter of the final word goes
processed food is mixed and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
ate without its last letter

explanation.surface: Pigs gobbled up endless amounts of processed food.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is long thin pasta, an example of a food.

clue.text: Irregular tactics foolishly ignored, crucial trial gets overturned

indicators.note: ignored takes letters away, and foolishly says they leave in any order, not as a run
overturned means upset and thrown about, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Unorthodox tactics, foolishly disregarded, cause a vital trial to be overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike the letters of TACTICS from CRUCIAL TRIAL GETS, scattered through it, and RULRIALGE remains to be rearranged. 'Irregular tactics' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Irregular'.
explanation.definitionFit: An irregular is a soldier outside the regular army, which is what a guerrilla fighter is.

clue.text: Boycotted regularly by head of theatre group

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept
the head of something is its top, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
first letter

explanation.surface: A theatre manager regularly shuns a musical group.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, especially eight musicians playing together.

clue.text: Fishing-boat in South America returns every time

indicators.note: in places the boat inside the continent's abbreviation
returning means coming back, so the whole is read from right to left

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for South
a yawl is a small sailing boat
A is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A fishing boat comes back to South America on every voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Always means on every occasion without exception, so it means every time.

clue.text: Primarily water snakes consuming large ducks?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so just the opening letter is used
consuming means swallowing up, so the snakes go around the other letter

blocks.note: first letter
adders are venomous snakes
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Water snakes swallowing big ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: ducks are birds that waddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks walk with a rolling, side-to-side gait, so they are things that waddle.

clue.text: Communication network having rejected gold standard

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the gold chemical symbol sitting inside the standard is read the other way round

blocks.note: a LAN is a local area network
a gauge is a standard of measurement, with Au, the symbol for gold, in its middle

explanation.surface: A communications network abandons the gold standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold standard' reads as one phrase, but gold is only the symbol already inside the standard, turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Language is the system of words people use to communicate, so it is communication itself.

clue.text: Most of ersatz British and German beer is cheaper

indicators.note: most of means all but a little, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: something ersatz is fake, a sham
B is the abbreviation for British
Bier is the German word for beer

explanation.surface: Imitation British and German beers sell for less.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabbier means more worn-out and inferior, close to cheaper in the sense of tawdry.

clue.text: Time of day province cuts power

indicators.note: cutting into something splits it open, so the first pair goes inside the other word

blocks.note: might is power
D is the abbreviation for day
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A daily power cut hits a province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time of day' looks like the definition, but 'day' is needed for D.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight is twelve o'clock at night, a particular time.

clue.text: Art form chimp astonishingly grasps

indicators.note: what the phrase grasps is held within it, running across the word break

blocks.note: inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A chimpanzee surprises everyone by mastering a painting style.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is a painting technique of laying paint on thickly, a form of artistic practice.

clue.text: Heartless gallery destroyed textile pattern

indicators.note: with no heart, the middle letter of the word is taken out
destroyed means wrecked, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; its central L goes

explanation.surface: A vandal ripped the heart out of an art gallery and ruined a textile.
explanation.definitionFit: Argyle is a diamond-check knitting design, as seen on socks and sweaters.

clue.text: Stage play casually follows mounted soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means climbing upward, so the letters read bottom to top
follows means comes after, so the strumming comes second

blocks.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
to strum is to play a guitar idly

explanation.surface: A casual stage play comes after a display by cavalry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted soldiers' suggests cavalry, but mounted reverses OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform for a speaker or conductor, a kind of stage.

clue.text: Nice red wines run out initially having good scores

indicators.note: run out initially means the first letter leaves, and 'having' brings in a replacement

blocks.note: rouges is French for red wines, and Nice is in France
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Fine red wines from Nice are sold out after getting high ratings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' reads as pleasant, but it is the French city, so the wine word is French. 'Scores' looks like ratings; it means cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouges are deep grooves or scratches, which is what scores are as nouns.

clue.text: Showy person's impudence when going after workers' organisation

indicators.note: going after means placed behind, so the impudence word comes second

blocks.note: TU is a trade union
lip is cheeky talk

explanation.surface: A flashy person is cheeky in going after the trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulip is a dated slang word for a showy, flamboyant person, after the gaudy flower.

clue.text: Reserves, old soldiers and Lord Lieutenant making a stand

blocks.note: to reserve a table is to book it
TA is the Territorial Army, the former name of Britain's volunteer reserve force
LL is the abbreviation for Lord Lieutenant

explanation.surface: Reservists, veterans and a county's royal representative take a stand together.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lord Lieutenant is the monarch's representative in a British county. 'Making a stand' reads as resisting, but 'a stand' is a kiosk.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookstall is a stand or kiosk selling books and papers, as at a station.

clue.text: A motive Environment Agency overlooked for crime

indicators.note: what is overlooked is left out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
a motive is a reason
EA, the Environment Agency, the English regulator for the environment

explanation.surface: An environmental regulator has missed the motive behind a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Worrying son without father's sinning

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are removed from the sinning word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to trespass is to sin, as in the Lord's Prayer
pa is father, plus the S

explanation.surface: A worried son agonises over his father's sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressing means fretting or feeling anxious, so it is a synonym for worrying.

clue.text: Sticky substance found in biro's ink

indicators.note: found in says the answer is lying within the next words, across the break

blocks.note: inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Something sticky turns up in a ballpoint pen's ink.
explanation.walkthrough: A biro is the British everyday word for a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosin is the solid resin left from distilling turpentine, a tacky substance used on violin bows.

clue.text: Scoff when men thus iron pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters before it are a mess to be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone mocks men who press their trousers this way.
explanation.walkthrough: Scoff looks like a verb meaning mock, but it is British slang for food. Pants reads as underwear or trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoff as a noun is informal British for food, and nourishment is food that sustains.
